description:
The latest review found two remaining trust problems in metric and scope
communication. Result detail pages can show raw exact power-score precision in
hero values, for example `11,636.652993864305`, while adjacent explorer
surfaces show rounded scan values. The leaderboard home can also say
`5 ranked, 2 published unranked` and then `Full leaderboard scope has 7 ranked
platform IDs`, which contradicts its own count semantics.

This TODO closes the gap between raw audit precision, scan-readable display
precision, and corpus/ranking scope copy. It must preserve exact values for
receipts, exports, sorting, and audit trails while using readable formatting
and truthful count labels in the UI.

anti_patterns.dont: patch one sentence without adding count invariants for other filter states.
remove exact values entirely just to simplify display.
round raw data before computing ranks, ratios, or comparisons.

preserves.behavior: Exact precision must remain available in receipt/audit contexts when it was previously available.
Leaderboard copy must match the filtered data actually rendered.
Raw metric values must remain unchanged in data, sorting, comparison math, and exports.
Scope count changes must not hide unranked or unpublished states.

work_units.notes:
Define explicit formatting rules:
  - scan contexts such as hero cards, leaderboard cells, chart labels, and
    compare cards use compact rounded values with meaningful significant
    digits;
  - comparison contexts keep enough precision for ratios and deltas without
    showing raw binary/float noise;
  - audit contexts such as receipts, exports, exact-value titles, and raw
    JSON retain exact source values.
Decision gate: do not use `fmtScoreExact` in scan contexts unless the UI
labels the value as exact and provides a reason for the precision.
